prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: whiplash. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1185; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on this, but you can use the case caption. Let's just say I'm the plaintiff in this matter.

Q: Understood. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving home from the grocery store in Pearland, Texas. It was in the late afternoon and the road was wet from a light rain.

Q: Describe what happened.

A: I was in the left lane heading north when a vehicle coming south crossed the center line and hit my front end. It wasn't a high-speed impact. I'd guess we were both going maybe twenty-five miles an hour, but the airbags didn't deploy. Still, my head snapped forward and then back.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head on anything?

A: No. I didn't black out and I didn't strike the windshield or the steering wheel. My neck just jerked hard.

Q: What did you do immediately after the collision?

A: I stayed in the car for a minute because my neck felt stiff. Then I got out, and the other driver was already on the phone. An officer came out and took our information. I remember thinking I'd be sore the next day, but I didn't expect it to last.

Q: When did you first seek medical care?

A: That evening, my neck and upper back were tight and I had a headache at the base of my skull. I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning because it was getting worse, not better.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?

A: I've had physical therapy two or three times a week for several months. I also got a referral to a chiropractor, and I was prescribed muscle relaxers and anti-inflammatories. My doctor mentioned possibly needing an injection if the therapy didn't help.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's made simple things hard. I can't turn my head to check my blind spot without pain, so I've had to adjust how I drive. I stopped going to my weekly yoga class because bending forward aggravates it. Sleeping is difficult too. I usually wake up two or three times a night because I can't get comfortable.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I've missed a few days and had to leave early on others. My job involves a lot of computer work, and sitting for long periods makes the pain flare up.

Q: Do you have any prior neck or back complaints?

A: I had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that required a doctor or treatment. Before this accident, I could exercise and do my normal activities without much trouble.
